# Saccavibhaṅga Sutta (MN 141 (PTS MN iii 248))
**ID:** MN 141 (PTS MN iii 248)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Saccavibhaṅga Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** The Analysis of the Truths
**PTS:** MN iii 248
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/mn141
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
This exposition combines brief definitions with word-by-word exegeses for the first truth (*dukkha*) and the fourth truth (the noble eightfold path), while retaining standard formulaic summaries for the origin and cessation of suffering [Anālayo, Dawn of Abhidharma].
Furthermore, comparative analysis indicates that an *Ekottarika-āgama* parallel lacks the qualification "noble" (*ariya*), referring simply to "four truths" and highlighting the gradual development of doctrinal terminology [Shulman 2014].
Curated full parallels include DN 22, *Madhyama-āgama* 31 (MĀ 31), *Ekottarika-āgama* 27.1 (EĀ 27.1), and an individual Chinese translation, the *Sìdì jīng* (四諦經, T 32), with partial parallels in EĀ 12.1, MĀ 98, MN 10, and a Sanskrit fragment (SHT sutta11) [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed text reuse shows extensive internal sharing across §22–31 with DN 22, the *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), the *Ñāṇakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1), the *Sacca Saṁyutta* (SN 56), and the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus alignments also match the text with MĀ 31 and T 32 (agreeing with SuttaCentral), as well as with Sanskrit and Tibetan versions of the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and the Sarvāstivāda *Dharmaskandha* [DharmaNexus].
